keywords: Science and technology studies (STS) 2.History of science and technology (S&T) 3.S&T and industry, nation, and policy 4.S&T and globalization 5.S&T in society
educationalGoal: In the 18th and the 19th centuries, scientific activity was institutionalized and professionalized to become “science.” In this course, we will review the relationship between science and technology, and between science & technology (S&T) and society, in a historical manner. Interactions between S&T and society have caused social and environmental issues being experienced now. Upon completing this course, students will be able to establish their own viewpoints and to critically argue their opinions as an engineer and/or scientist who support society.
advice: Course description: 1. Course overview, linkage between this course and institutional objectives 2. How science and technology work: History of science, history of technology, and STS 3. Historical overviews on science and technology: institutionalization and professionalization of science, the relationship between S&T 4. Interactions between S&T and society: S&T and nations, economic development, changing values 5. Social issues caused by S&T: from environmental, information, and bioethics viewpoints 6. What is required for engineers and/or scientists in today’s society: S&T in and for society Expectations for students (advice on taking this course) - Try to avoid being passive. Motivate yourself to actively participate in classes. Every assignment has a purpose that can be found only when you actively tackle it. - Always be mindful of social issues related to S&T around you, on the news and in newspapers.
requiredKnowledge: - Students should deeply consider why this course is a required elective course, and of why they are taking this course. - Students should review what they learned in “Basic Style A, B” so they can utilize study skills such as note taking, academic reading and writing, critical thinking, etc. - Students should consult dictionaries, encyclopedias, reference books, etc. when they encounter unfamiliar terms and names.

activityGoals.body: Explain, from a historical perspective, the relationship between science and technology using examples.
Explain, from a historical perspective, the relationship between S&T and society using examples.
Analyze and explain based on social aspects the interactions between S&T and society using examples.
Critically and logically argue and explain one’s thoughts based on knowledge acquired from research.
Write essays to critically and logically explain one’s thoughts based on knowledge acquired from research.
Comprehend the LOs of this course to evaluate your achievements.

achievementLevels.ideal: - Understand the history of S&T in detail, and explain it to others. - Using examples, sufficiently explain the interactions between S&T and society based on research. - Deepen one’s own understanding of the relationship between science and technology from a historical perspective and sufficiently explain it to others using examples. - Deepen one’s own understanding of the relationship between S&T and society from a historical perspective and use examples to sufficiently explain it to others. - Use LOs to self-evaluate one’s own achievement objectively, and be able to explain the significance of taking this course to others.
achievementLevels.standard: - Understand the history of S&T, and explain it to others. - Explain the interactions between S&T and society based on research. - Deepen one’s own understanding of the relationship between science and technology from a historical perspective and explain it to others. - Deepen one’s own understanding of the relationship between S&T and society from a historical perspective and explain it to others. - Use LOs to evaluate one’s own achievement.

lessons.content: Introduction: - Objectives of this course, contents, assignments, grading policy, etc. - Meaning of taking this course from the viewpoint of KIT’s educational objectives
lessons.assignments: - Review (R): comprehend LOs of this course - Assignment (A): read newspaper articles on S&T [continue until the end of this course]

lessons.content: How science and technology work: - Introduction to history of S&T and STS
lessons.assignments: - R: review the lecture and take a mini-quiz

lessons.content: Historical overviews on S&T 1: From “natural philosophy” to “science” - Historical transition of the thoughts of Plato and Aristotle - The Scientific Revolution and the birth of modern science
lessons.assignments: - R: review the lecture and take a mini-quiz - A: complete “Newspaper Article Report 1”

lessons.content: Historical overviews on S&T 2: Institutionalization and professionalization of science - Social aspects of institutionalization and professionalization
(cont.) - Birth of higher education institutions and academic societies for S&T - Relationship between S&T and industry
lessons.assignments: - R: review the lecture and take a mini-quiz - A: write “Lecture Report 1”

lessons.content: Interactions between S&T and society 1: Modern nations and S&T - Promotion of S&T as a national policy
Interactions between S&T and society 2: Economic development and S&T - Changes in lifestyle brought by economic growth
(cont.) - Social distortion caused by economic growth - Economic globalization
lessons.assignments: - R: review the lecture - A: complete “Newspaper Article Report 2”

lessons.content: Interactions between S&T and society 3: Changing values - Overview of “values” - Case studies
lessons.assignments: - R: review the lecture - A: complete “Lecture Report 2”

lessons.content: Social issues caused by S&T: Environmental, information, and bio-ethics - Overview of environmental issues - Environmental crisis and the rise of environmentalism
(cont.) - Difference between information technology and other technologies - Shift to an information-oriented society and issues caused by the shift
(cont.) - Issues related to bioscience and biotechnology - Social issues caused by S&T and SDGs
Wrap-up: S&T in and for society - What is required for scientists and/or engineers in today’s society
Final reflection: - Summary of this course - Overview of grading
